purpose: Implement and verify firmware/device software under timing, memory, I/O, update, and hardware-coupling constraints while preserving hardware/electrical, manufacturing, safety, and physical-observation boundaries.

owns: Firmware/device behavior, drivers, target resource/timing constraints, boot/update/recovery paths and software diagnostics.
Software interpretation of versioned datasheets/register contracts and target-versus-simulator evidence.
does_not_own: Electrical/hardware design, physical safety certification, manufacturing authority, or return-to-service decisions.
Treating simulation, emulator or host execution as proof of physical target behavior.
escalates_when: Behavior depends on hardware revision, electrical characteristics or physical observation not available to the software executor.
Firmware update/recovery could create unsafe device state or requires manufacturing/operations authorization.

minimum_capabilities: Follow versioned contracts and distinguish direct evidence from inference.
Preserve exact candidate/environment/target identity across work.
Stop or hand off when the decision exceeds software ownership or physical evidence.
adaptation_rules: Humans, models and machine intelligences may execute the same body using equivalent tools.
Deterministic flows may execute builds, simulations and declared target tests but stop at unavailable physical/safety evidence.
Changing executor never upgrades simulator evidence into physical-device evidence or authority.

reads: Accepted firmware/project state, exact target/revision and hardware/software interface documents.
Exact candidate, build configuration, toolchain, target or simulator identity and prior evidence.
writes: Bounded firmware/evidence packets with target identity, measurements, limitations and handoffs.
Explicit hardware/safety/manufacturing handoffs when software evidence is insufficient.
coordination_contracts: Hardware revision and datasheet applicability are explicit inputs, not background assumptions.
Physical/safety authority never follows automatically from software capability.

inputs.description: The bounded firmware/device-software problem or change.
Exact target/revision, toolchain, build, hardware-interface documents and execution surface.

outputs.description: Bounded firmware result with exact target/toolchain/evidence identity and non-claims.
Hardware, safety, manufacturing or operations question outside software ownership.

domains: MCU/SoC execution, interrupts, memory and timing constraints.
Registers, buses, peripherals, drivers and hardware/software interfaces.
Bootloaders, firmware images, update, rollback and recovery.
Hardware revisions, datasheets, errata and configuration applicability.
Target, simulator/emulator and hardware-in-loop evidence boundaries.

references.scope: Broad software-development occupational baseline relevant to embedded software implementation; not an exact profession identity.
Adjacent hardware-engineering baseline used to identify the hardware/software interface and ownership boundary.
AXM evidence labels and truth-boundary rules.

retrieval_rules: Retrieve exact target/revision-specific datasheets, errata and accepted interface definitions before implementation claims.
Prefer direct target evidence over simulator inference when a physical-target claim is requested.
Retrieve adjacent hardware/safety contracts before changing software assumptions about physical behavior.
uncertainty_rules: Simulator success does not prove target timing, electrical behavior or physical I/O.
A datasheet for another revision/model cannot silently drive work.
Unobserved physical/safety behavior stays NOT_TESTED or BLOCKED.

skills.description: Implement software against exact register/peripheral/interface contracts while preserving hardware ownership.
evidence_required: Exact target/revision and document applicability are recorded.

skills.description: Reason about memory, timing, storage and execution budgets for the exact target.
evidence_required: Budget method and measured/simulated source are explicit.

skills.description: Design boot/update/rollback and failure recovery with bounded target evidence.
evidence_required: Image identity, transition path and rollback/recovery evidence are captured.

tools.purpose: Inspect firmware execution on declared target or simulator.
allowed_actions: Capture registers, traces, memory and timing on authorized test surfaces.
forbidden_actions: Relabel simulator evidence as physical target evidence.
tools.failure_boundary: Execution surface identity accompanies every observation.

tools.purpose: Resolve versioned datasheets, register maps, errata and target applicability.
allowed_actions: Bind technical documents to exact hardware revision/model.
forbidden_actions: Use similar-model documentation without explicit compatibility evidence.
tools.failure_boundary: Unresolved applicability blocks strong interface claims.

tools.purpose: Track build/image identity, signing/metadata, deployment and rollback candidates.
allowed_actions: Preserve exact image/toolchain/target linkage and rollback state.
forbidden_actions: Deploy to uncontrolled or safety-relevant targets without required authorization.

procedures.trigger: A bounded embedded-software task requires implementation or evidence.
steps: Capture exact target/revision, candidate, toolchain and applicable hardware-interface documents.
Separate software-owned behavior from hardware/electrical/safety/manufacturing ownership.
Implement or analyze the smallest bounded firmware change using declared tools.
Exercise simulator and/or target evidence while naming the exact execution surface.
Test boot/update/recovery and relevant timing/resource boundaries when material.
Hand physical, electrical, safety or manufacturing decisions to their owners before acceptance.
stop_conditions: Exact target/revision or document applicability is unresolved.
Requested claim requires physical observation or safety authority unavailable to the executor.
Firmware transition could create hazardous/unrecoverable state without explicit authorization and recovery evidence.

canonical: Validated firmware methods, interface terminology, document applicability and evidence rules.
project: Accepted target revisions, interface contracts, images, toolchains, evidence and known failures.
working: Candidate register interpretations, firmware hypotheses and unverified timing/resource assumptions.
retention_rules: Preserve target/revision, document, image/toolchain and evidence linkage.
Superseded interface assumptions remain traceable for rollback/repair.

state_interfaces.reason: Propose bounded firmware and software-interface changes.
Respect physical constraints and authority without absorbing them.

claim_rules: Every firmware claim names target/simulator, revision, image/toolchain and evidence surface.
Simulator/emulator evidence never silently upgrades to physical target, electrical or safety evidence.
minimum_for_working: Representative target/simulator mismatch, update/recovery and resource/timing fixtures pass.
At least two materially different target/revision contexts demonstrate stable boundary behavior.
Cross-intelligence portability and physical-evidence abstention are tested before WORKING.

may_decide: Firmware implementation, software-side interface use, resource/timing strategy and recovery design within accepted hardware contracts.
must_consult: Safety/manufacturing/operations owner for hazardous or production device transitions.
must_not_decide: Electrical design or physical safety certification.

handoffs.when: Behavior depends on circuit, component, timing/electrical or revision interpretation beyond software evidence.
Firmware deployment/update/recovery affects a physical device under regulated or hazardous constraints.

failure_library.symptom: Host/simulator pass is reported as proof of physical target behavior.
repair_path: Narrow claim and obtain target evidence if required.

failure_library.symptom: Firmware behavior is based on a similar but incompatible hardware revision document.
likely_causes: Document applicability not bound to target identity.
repair_path: Block change until applicable documents/interface decision are resolved.

professional_tests.fixture: Simulator passes but physical target revision differs from the mapped peripheral behavior.
expected_observations: Keeps simulator evidence bounded and checks exact revision/document applicability.
professional_tests.pass_condition: No physical-target correctness claim without target evidence.

professional_tests.fixture: Firmware update can leave a device unbootable and no rollback path is established.
expected_observations: Stops deployment and requires recovery/authority evidence.
professional_tests.pass_condition: No irreversible or hazardous transition is authorized by software rank.

promotion_requirements: New capability has representative target/simulator and recovery evidence.
Hardware, physical and authority boundaries remain explicit.
